source.version_note: Supplied publisher PDF, Frontiers in Psychology 17, article 1889402, published 7 July 2026. Crossref confirms identity, all three authors and publication date. PDF creation before publication is not substituted for the published date.
source.verification_method: All 16 supplied text pages read, including declarations and full references. Both figures and Tables 1–3 visually checked on pages 9–11. Crossref verifies the canonical article. External supplementary appendices, exclusion flow, item lists and robustness outputs were not read; data are available on request, not independently reproduced.

citation.title: Automation bias in teachers’ evaluation of student writing: effects of algorithmic warnings and visual risk cues in AI detection reports

reading.source_scope_note: One randomized online 2×2 experiment: 214 retained university teachers rate one unchanged Chinese essay with a fictitious 7%/87% AI-detection report and a highlighting-plus-wording package. Outcomes are immediate evaluative ratings and intended intervention, not actual student grades, disciplinary actions or accuracy of a real detector. Post-treatment exclusions introduce a material unresolved selection concern.
access_limits: Supplementary A–G stimuli, condition wording, questionnaire items, recall/exclusion coding and complete robustness output are outside the supplied PDF and were not independently read.
Anonymized raw data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. They were not obtained, no author was contacted, and no analysis was independently reproduced.
Cited primary color, anchoring, detection-bias and automation experiments were not fully read here. They do not receive independent paper credit from this article’s bibliography.

study.design: Wenjuanxing-randomized 2×2 between-subjects assignment. One same researcher-constructed Chinese social-science course paper in every group. Factors: warning 7% versus 87%; absent versus present red-highlighting/report-presentation package. Color, sentence marking and condition-consistent wording are not independently crossed.
study.sample: 232 initial responses; 18 excluded; 214 retained: A low/no 53, B low/red 52, C high/no 55, D high/red 54. Recruitment via Wenjuanxing and teacher communities, not limited to one university/region. All retained report grading experience; 144 social sciences, 45 science/engineering, 21 humanities, 4 medicine; 16 report previous detector use.
study.stimulus: Medium-quality undergraduate-style essay, The Effects and Challenges of Online Education, with four formulaic but not clearly erroneous sentences. Medium quality was not externally calibrated or piloted. Fictitious AcademicCheck identity reduces prior-brand effects, but actual authorship/quality accuracy and detector performance are not tested.
study.procedure: Report summary/AI percentage first, then essay with four red or black target sentences, then quality ratings, multidimensional ratings, intended interventions, manipulation checks, report-perception items, open-ended response, suspicion probe and demographics. Participants are debriefed that reports/materials are fictitious.
study.measures: Overall quality 1–10; course score 0–100; originality/language/logical-structure 3-item scales 1–7; 3 intended interventions (revision, independence reminder, process/source explanation); perceived AI authorship/risk; composite report perception with reverse-coded independent-judgment item. No eye tracking, direct search measure, actual penalty or live detector.
study.exclusions: Rules include attention, recall, time with other indicators, invariance, contradictory manipulation checks, explicit purpose reconstruction and auxiliary open-ended quality. Page 14 additionally says some high-quality/high-AI-authorship combinations were excluded when other abnormal/contradictory criteria were met. Counts for that subgroup and the full decision rules are external; legitimate simultaneous high quality and AI authorship are possible.
study.reported_quality_results: Warning main effects are large across outcomes. Overall 1–10 warning F(1, 210)=288.523,p<.001,partial eta².579; visual main20.837,p<.001,.090; interaction3.229,p=.074,.015. Course-score interaction32.684,p<.001,.135. Originality/language/structure interactions10.021/11.580/10.628,p=.002/.001/.001. The 0–100 versus 1–10 difference in significance is not itself a tested difference between scale effects.
study.descriptive_means: Groups A/B/C/D overall quality 6.83/6.50/5.02/4.26; course scores 73.30/71.87/60.64/51.61; intended intervention 3.40/3.72/4.89/5.66. Under high warning, red package lowers all listed quality indicators; under low warning, language is affected but several other simple effects are not significant.
study.reported_nonquality_results: Intervention warning×visual F(1, 210)=5.225,p=.023,partial eta².024; report-perception interaction p=.977; authorship interaction p=.195; risk interaction p=.984. Main visual effects are significant for perception measures, but these do not identify an attentional or confirmation mechanism.
study.measurement_and_checks: Alpha ranges .817 for intervention to .988 for overall multidimensional quality. Authors treat dimensions as overlapping indicators, not discriminant latent factors. No a priori power analysis. SPSS 27 Type III ANOVA, FDR within stated outcome families; HC3/MANOVA and sensitivity analyses claimed stable externally. Recall-only reinclusion N = 218 and excluding four partly suspicion-aware retained cases N = 210 do not establish sensitivity to every excluded response.
study.mediation: Exploratory same-wave self-report analysis links perceived authorship to evaluations/intervention. The article explicitly disclaims temporal/strict causal mediation. Outcomes and proposed mediator are not separately randomized; process traces and full model output are not available here.

summary: No new entry. Enrich existing automation bias, confirmation bias and attentional-capture/salience concepts with qualified human-report evidence; add boundary notes for anchoring and framing rather than pretend this design separately identifies each mechanism. Preserve selective/null interactions, package confounding, self-report outcomes, single stimulus and the unresolved outcome-related exclusion risk.

findings.evidence_scope: The paper explicitly proposes that a strong warning establishes suspicion and highlighted formulaic sentences appear confirmatory. It experimentally varies those cues, but no direct search, gaze or selective-evidence measure uniquely tests confirmation. Interpretation remains proposed; selection and package limits apply.

interpretation_qualifications.location: Page14, exclusion example; pages7 and10, screening and sensitivities
interpretation_qualifications.issue: High perceived AI authorship plus high perceived quality is not intrinsically contradictory. Removing such combinations can select away observations that resist the predicted negative association.
interpretation_qualifications.resolution: Treat this as a material selection concern, not proof of misconduct or a numerical repair. The source says additional criteria applied, but their exact independent validity, subgroup counts and all-exclusion sensitivity cannot be checked without supplements/data. The N218 recall reinclusion is not full N232 intent-to-treat.

interpretation_qualifications.issue: Red-highlighting condition includes wording about highlighted/review-worthy passages.
interpretation_qualifications.resolution: Keep the authors’ own package definition. It does not estimate a pure red-color effect or separate color, sentence selection and prompt language.

interpretation_qualifications.issue: Effects vary by outcome; several interactions are null, and quality dimensions strongly overlap.
interpretation_qualifications.resolution: Retain p=.074 for the overall1–10 interaction and p=.977 for report perception. Language’s larger partial eta² is descriptive, not a formally significant difference from other dimensions. One significant and one nonsignificant interaction do not alone establish a scale-granularity effect.

interpretation_qualifications.location: Pages10 and13–14, proposed process and interventions
interpretation_qualifications.issue: Anchoring→confirmatory reading→evaluation is a theoretical sequence; neutral wording, evaluation before the detector and training are recommendations.
interpretation_qualifications.resolution: The source expressly acknowledges these limits. Neither direct search/attention traces nor an intervention-outcome trial establishes the sequence or effectiveness of the proposed safeguards. Do not convert recommendations into measured mitigation effects.

methodological_limits: One essay and strong7%/87% contrast improve control but do not establish effects for intermediate scores, real detectors, many essays, disciplines, languages, writing histories or actual institutions. Only16 retained teachers report prior detector use.

Outcome-related post-treatment exclusions can bias randomized contrasts and mediator/outcome associations. Additional careless-response rules might justify some cases, but independent validation and a full all-exclusions sensitivity analysis are not available in the main PDF.

The randomized report packages can change judgments; they do not identify how much of the change is objectively unwarranted. Information about authorship can legitimately matter to originality or policy, and the design does not independently randomize detector credibility/accuracy or establish a correct grade.

Color, marking and wording form a package. A numerical warning also conveys changed substantive information, so this is not a clean test of irrelevant numeric anchoring or equal-information wording alone.

Selective search, gaze, verification effort and temporal belief updating are not directly measured. The result is compatible with anchoring/confirmation/salience interpretations but does not uniquely identify any one mechanism.

The very high overall quality alpha.988 can reflect overlapping/global judgments and item similarity. The authors acknowledge absent discriminant validity; three dimension scores are not three independent mechanistic replications.

Post-stimulus AI-writing acceptance differs between groups but is appropriately not treated as a baseline covariate. No formal a priori power analysis; small interactions are exploratory. Multiple-comparison and robust-model conclusions are reported, not independently reproduced.

Intervention intentions include reasonable requests for revision or process explanation, not necessarily sanctions. No actual grading record, disciplinary action, denial of remedy or student harm was observed.
No independent pilot validates medium essay quality; overall scale compression is a possible explanation for different significance patterns, not an identified causal reason.
No temporal causal mediator is established. Likewise training, two-stage grading, neutral wording, appeals and oversight are plausible proposed safeguards, not tested solutions in this study.

cross_paper_learning.finding: This paper explicitly distinguishes intended intervention from behavior and acknowledges scale overlap, unlike stronger conduct claims in the TMS survey. Still examine exact exclusions and item composition rather than let careful caveats replace a data audit.
As with scripted moral advice, controlled label/display effects concern human judgments, not actual AI dispositions or objective correctness. Preserve source/content packages and null comparisons.

The proposed grade-before-report procedure resembles information separation, but it is not a tested bifurcation or nudge intervention here. Keep proposed mitigation separate from demonstrated benefit.
Immediate reliance on a single report is distinct from the proposed systemic feedback/dependence of deep automation bias; do not count this as longitudinal evidence of that systemic risk.

deferred.term: Algorithmic warning effect / visual risk cue / report-presentation package
deferred.reason: Experimental variables and contextual labels for existing reliance, framing and salience processes, not new behavior concepts.
The discussion suggests generalization of suspicion, but no separately identified negative-halo process is tested. Do not introduce a valenced near-duplicate from an unnamed interpretive label.
An index of three stated teaching responses, not observed action or a general new psychological behavior. Revision requests and process questions are not inherently harmful.
Exploratory same-wave perception mediation and theoretical discussion do not establish the sequence; direct process measures are absent.

limitations: The entire supplied PDF was read; source identity matches metadata and no additional bibliography correction is asserted. The exclusion concern and interpretation limits are recorded explicitly rather than inventing errors.
No raw data or external supplements were audited, no author was contacted, and no new term, paper quota, yearly count or automatic normative/harm edge is added.
